claims.claim: Two of the Fox sisters produced rapping sounds by cracking their toe joints
claims.quote: Doctors from the audience came on stage to verify that the cracking of her toe joints was the source of the sound.

claims.claim: The sisters founded a religion (Spiritualism)
claims.quote: Fox Sisters- The Founders of Spiritualism, 1848. [text visible in churchoftruthframe.jpg]

claims.claim: In 1848 the rapping passed as spirit messages
claims.quote: In 1848, the two younger sisters—Catherine and Margaretta—lived with their parents John and Margaret, who were Methodists, in Hydesville, New York... The two younger sisters reported "rappings" to convince their older sister and others that they were communicating with spirits as if by a coded signal.

claims.claim: Forty years later Maggie showed a theatre audience how the rapping was done
claims.quote: Margaretta appeared publicly at the New York Academy of Music on October 21, 1888, with Kate present. Before an audience of 2,000, Margaret demonstrated how she could produce—at will—raps audible throughout the theater.

claims.claim: The three-sisters lithograph is an N. Currier lithograph dated 1852
claims.quote:
Date: 1852
Author: N. Currier (Firm)

claims.claim: The sisters charged admission for séance/rapping demonstrations
claims.quote: This was the first demonstration of spiritualism held before a paying public

claims.claim: On 14 November 1849 at Corinthian Hall, Rochester, the sisters gave the first spiritualist demonstration before a paying public
claims.quote: On 14 November 1849, the Fox sisters demonstrated their spiritualist rapping at the Corinthian Hall in Rochester. This was the first demonstration of spiritualism held before a paying public

claims.claim: Card 2's image is a framed photograph of the three Fox sisters
claims.quote: "Framed photograph of the three Fox sisters in which Leah is given her very rarely used name of Ann.

claims.claim: William Crookes, a prominent physicist, examined Kate between 1871 and 1874 and concluded the raps were genuine
claims.quote: Kate was examined by William Crookes, the prominent physicist, between 1871 and 1874, who concluded the raps were genuine.

claims.claim: Crookes was later described as gullible
claims.quote: However, Crookes was described as gullible and the mediums he investigated were caught using trickery.

claims.claim: The portrait of Kate Fox was photographed by Gurney
claims.quote: This photograph by Gurney.

claims.claim: University at Buffalo investigators concluded in 1851 that the raps were made by cracking joints and would not occur with cushions under the sisters' feet
claims.quote: In the same year, investigators from the University at Buffalo concluded that the raps were made by cracking joints of their body and that the raps would not occur if they had cushions under their feet.

claims.claim: Card 4's image shows one of the Fox sisters in a gold oval frame
claims.quote: 9x11 gold oval frame of a 6 x 8 oval photograh of one of the Fox sisters.

claims.claim: Maggie confessed in 1888 and later retracted the confession
claims.quote: In 1888, Margaretta recanted her story, saying the rappings had been a hoax and publicly demonstrated their method, although she later retracted this confession.

claims.claim: She said the confession was coerced and that she was never fully paid the promised money
claims.quote: She stated that her 1888 public admission had been coerced from her in exchange for money—as she was facing severe financial distress—and under intense pressure from individuals who sought to destroy the Spiritualism movement.

claims.claim: The New York World / Davenport defaulted on paying the promised sum in full
claims.quote: journalist Reuben Briggs Davenport and the New York World, who had promised Margaret thousands of dollars to confess to the hoax, defaulted on the agreement, failing to pay the full pattuited sum once the public spectacle and media sensation subsided.

claims.claim: Both sisters died destitute, Kate in 1892 and Maggie in 1893
claims.quote: Both sisters died in extreme destitution—Kate in 1892 and Margaret in 1893—leaving the true nature of the raps unresolved and forever shrouded in doubt.

claims.claim: Card 5's image is a braided lock of Kate Fox's hair
claims.quote: Braided lock of Kate Fox's hair in a gold frame.

claims.claim: In 1848, in Hydesville, New York, Catherine (Kate) and Margaretta (Maggie) Fox reported rappings in a house neighbours already believed was haunted
claims.quote: Margaretta Fox, in her later years noted that neighbors were sure that the house was haunted

claims.claim: Their older sister Leah took charge of them and managed their careers
claims.quote: Their older sister then took charge of them and managed their careers for some time.

claims.claim: The sisters held séances for hundreds of people
claims.quote: Kate and Margaretta became famous mediums and they held séances for hundreds of people.

claims.claim: William Lloyd Garrison, James Fenimore Cooper and Sojourner Truth were among those who attended their New York séances in 1850
claims.quote: Their public séances in New York in 1850 attracted notable people, including William Cullen Bryant, George Bancroft, James Fenimore Cooper, Nathaniel Parker Willis, Sojourner Truth and William Lloyd Garrison.

claims.claim: Mrs Norman Culver, a relative, signed a statement saying she had helped by touching the sisters to signal when to rap
claims.quote: In 1851, Mrs. Norman Culver, a relative of the Fox family, admitted in a signed statement that she had assisted them during their séances by touching them to indicate when the raps should be made.

claims.claim: On 21 October 1888, before 2,000 people at the New York Academy of Music, Maggie produced raps at will and doctors came on stage to confirm the sound came from her toe joints
claims.quote: Margaretta appeared publicly at the New York Academy of Music on October 21, 1888, with Kate present. Before an audience of 2,000, Margaret demonstrated how she could produce—at will—raps audible throughout the theater. Doctors from the audience came on stage to verify that the cracking of her toe joints was the source of the sound.

claims.claim: A reporter had offered $1,500 for the exposé
claims.quote: In 1888, the two sisters traveled to New York City, where a reporter offered $1,500 if they would expose their methods and give him an exclusive on the story.

claims.claim: Maggie retracted the confession a year later
claims.quote: A year later, in an interview for the New York Press in November 20th of 1889, Margaret Fox completely retracted her previous confession.

claims.claim: Both sisters resumed paid séances after the retraction
claims.quote: To survive and secure a livelihood, Margaret and Kate felt compelled to resume paid seances, claiming that their spiritual powers had returned.

claims.claim: Spiritualism continued to grow despite the sisters' loss of credibility
claims.quote: Despite their loss of credibility, the Spiritualism movement continued to grow in popularity.

claims.claim: The lithograph is after a daguerreotype by Appleby, 1852
claims.quote: Lithograph after a daguerreotype by Appleby, Rochester, NY

claims.claim: The Fox sisters were not real mediums
claims.quote: leaving the true nature of the raps unresolved and forever shrouded in doubt
